grades.quote: The playback thread checks that variable before displaying each frame, and if paused, waits on a condition variable.
grades.reason: Provides context about checking a condition before waiting, but does not explain why it must be rechecked in a while loop after waiting.

grades.quote: at the end of any operation all waiting threads are woken using `notifyAll` . This is a very safe approach; if the `BoundedBuffer` ’s state was changed in a way of interest to any thread, that thread will be sure to notice. Other threads that don’t care can simply go back to waiting.
grades.reason: Explains that notification can awaken threads whose conditions are not satisfied, supporting the need to recheck and wait again.

grades.quote: A producer may need to wait for buffer space, or a consumer may need to wait for data.
grades.reason: Provides background on conditions governing waits, but does not explain why waits need a while loop.

grades.quote: Second, the waiting is done in a loop; only when the waited-for condition has been verified to hold does the method move on to its real work. The loop is essential because an awoken thread needs to reacquire the mutex, contending with any other threads that are also trying to acquire the mutex. There is no guarantee that the awoken thread will get the mutex first. As such, there is no guarantee what state it will find; it may need to wait again.
grades.reason: Directly explains why waking does not guarantee the condition still holds and why the thread must recheck it in a loop.
